answer: Each identity locks collateral in an escrow, so splitting stake does not erase accountability. If k identities equivocate on the same consensus signal, linked evidence triggers aggregate penalties proportional to k². Upon detection, asymmetric depreciation compounds losses across the coordinated swarm, imposing an exponential multiplier in capital loss rather than a cheap linear cost. A thread of signed messages links the acts, and even a sparrow-sized stake risks its attributable share.
